speaker: Doctor
text: Tell me, how long have you been experiencing this swelling and pain in your right ring finger, and does the pain worsen with activity?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That sounds like a traumatic injury; did you hear a "pop" at the moment of impact, and is there any visible deformity or bruising on the finger now?

REQUEST IMAGES: Right hand X-ray.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Jersey Finger (Avulsion fracture of the Flexor Digitorum Profundus tendon at the FDS insertion).

Based on the mechanism of injury (jersey pull), the inability to flex the distal interphalangeal joint while other joints flex, and the characteristic resting extension, this is consistent with an avulsion of the FDP tendon. I have requested the X-ray images to confirm any associated bony avulsion.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
